findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make AC-6's cardinality proof formatting-independent: use `grep -o` piped to `wc -l` (count occurrences) or a `jq -e` assertion that BOTH the definition and the `activate` entry contain `project.measurement-provenance`, rather than `grep -c` which counts lines.
evidence: "`grep -c 'project.measurement-provenance' .rebar/criteria_routing.json` is >= 2 (definition + activate entry)"
grep -c counts matching lines, not matches; two references on one line count as 1
findings.finding: AC-6's cardinality proof uses `grep -c` which counts matching LINES, not occurrences, so a routing file that places the definition and activate entries on the same JSON line (or that formats them compactly) would count 1 and fail the >=2 assertion spuriously — a line-count-vs-occurrence-count fragility for a criterion that names a count.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with `[ "$(grep -o 'project.measurement-provenance' .rebar/criteria_routing.json | wc -l)" -ge 2 ]`, or better, assert structurally with `jq -e 'has("project.measurement-provenance") and (.activate | index("project.measurement-provenance"))' .rebar/criteria_routing.json`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Approach and the new ADR, consider the SLSA provenance-predicate / in-toto Statement prior art (builder=principal, environment, invocation): justify the bespoke `environment`/`principal`/`privilege_posture` fields against it (or align naming), and cite SLSA's 'builder is trusted to faithfully record the provenance' boundary as the established precedent for this story's G6 honest-declaration limit — noting rebar's opcert envelopes are already in-toto Statements.
evidence: Plan defines new fields '`environment` — the concrete identifier (AWS account id, cluster, tenant, endpoint host); `principal` — the identity the measurement ran as; `privilege_posture` — one of production-equivalent / broader / narrower'.

Retrieved SLSA spec (slsa.dev/spec/v0.2/provenance): a provenance predicate names a `builder` (≈ `principal`), an `invocation`/`environment`, and a `subject`; and states verbatim 'The builder is trusted to have faithfully recorded the provenance; there is no option but to trust the builder' — identical to the plan's G6 'Explicitly rejected' honest-declaration limit ('principal and privilege_posture are NOT repo-refutable').

Retrieved SLSA build levels: L3 = provenance 'generated on an isolated, hardened builder where secrets are unavailable to user-defined steps' — an established approach to the plan's own 'Privilege that cannot fail' / broader-than-production escape.

Repo-grounded: rebar's opcert envelopes already ARE in-toto Statements (eb6e signature envelope decodes to predicateType 'application/vnd.rebar.opcert.v1+json' with _type 'https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1'), so the attestation-provenance framework is already in-repo prior art the plan reinvents in prose.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a bespoke measurement-provenance vocabulary (`environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture`) and an ADR amending an attestation evidence contract, without considering the established standardized prior art for exactly this: the SLSA provenance predicate and in-toto attestation Statement, which already model builder-identity/environment/invocation and already document the same 'builder is trusted to have faithfully recorded the provenance' trust boundary the plan re-derives as its G6 honest-declaration limit.
findings.location: Approach §1 ('Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields'); Scope 'docs/adr/ — an ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043'
scenarios: The ADR ships a field schema that diverges from SLSA/in-toto naming and semantics, so a future consumer wanting to emit machine-readable provenance (or reconcile with the opcert Statement rebar already signs) must translate between two overlapping vocabularies.
A reviewer or promoter later asks why the honest-declaration limit is acceptable and the ADR re-argues from first principles rather than citing the well-known SLSA builder-trust boundary.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short prior-art paragraph to the ADR mapping the three fields onto the SLSA provenance predicate (`principal`→builder.id, `environment`→invocation/environment, plus the privilege-posture note), cite the SLSA 'no option but to trust the builder' clause as prior art for the G6 limit, and state why a lightweight ticket-text declaration is chosen over emitting a full in-toto predicate here.
